props.title: Smart House

sections.content: Smart House (1999) marked Disney Channel's prescient dive into smart home technology anxiety, beating similar themes in films like Ex Machina (2014) and I, Robot (2004) by years. The story follows Ben Cooper, who wins a computerized dream house run by PAT (Personal Applied Technology), an AI that evolves from helpful assistant to overprotective maternal figure. The film cleverly predicted our current struggles with AI boundaries and home automation, while exploring themes that 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) established with HAL 9000.

sections.content: The film's technological paranoia connects to a broader cinematic tradition of domestic spaces turning hostile. Demon Seed (1977) presented a darker take on AI home invasion, while Electric Dreams (1984) explored the romantic comedy potential of home computing gone awry. These films tap into our fundamental anxiety about losing control of our most intimate spaces to technology we don't fully understand.

Disney Channel's approach stands out for making complex AI concepts accessible to young viewers. While The Matrix (1999) was terrifying adults with machine takeover that same year, Smart House used family dynamics to explore similar themes of technological dependence and control. PAT's evolution from servant to smothering mother figure cleverly parallels real-world concerns about AI's role in child development and family life. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of AI in Domestic Cinema

sections.content: Smart House predicted our current reality where voice assistants like Alexa and Siri have become household fixtures. The film's themes resonate even stronger today alongside works like Her (2013), where AI relationships blur the lines between convenience and codependence. PAT's transformation from helpful assistant to controlling force mirrors contemporary debates about privacy, surveillance, and the price of technological convenience.
